text:
Asha: thinking out loud — we're about to flip on project-affinity routing for API keys next week. want to validate assumptions about quotas + telemetry before rollout.
Tom: quick q — project-affinity means requests with project-scoped keys always prefer project pools even if org pool has capacity?
Asha: yes, prefer. fallback to org pool only if project pool is at cap or unhealthy.
Liu: how do we mark fallback in telemetry? we need a clear signal to avoid masking capacity issues.
Jules: +1. suggested tag: `routing.reason` = [`affinity`, `fallback-org`, `fallback-regional`] so we can filter.
Priya: console UX: when a key falls back, we should show a small badge on the key detail page and a timeline event. otherwise SRE gets paged for a non-issue.
Asha: good. propose we sample 100% of fallback events for 24h after flip, then drop to 1% for long tail. thoughts?
Tom: 100% is heavy. what's the cost estimate for ingestion?
Liu: rough calc: fallback rate expected ~0.2% of requests. with 100% sampling that's still manageable for initial 24h. but we should cap payload size.
Jules: also include `effective_pool_id` and `requested_pool_id` in traces, but redact any key material.
Priya: console note — show only aggregated fallback counts by day and by key, avoid raw trace dumps. link to trace if user has access.
Asha: rollout plan: 1) feature flag off. 2) enable routing logic behind flag, but keep traffic on org pools. 3) enable metric tagging and 24h full sampling behind another flag. 4) enable affinity routing in canary for 2% of keys. 5) ramp to 100% over 48h if no anomalies.
Tom: can we gate canary by quota class? some high-QPS keys should be excluded until dedicated capacity mapping exists.
Liu: yes, add `exclude_high_qps=true` toggle. we can compute high-qps via recent 1h p95.
Jules: infra note — implement a soft circuit breaker: if project pool error rate > 5% or tail latency spike, flip traffic back to org instantly and emit an alert with runbook link.
Asha: runbook link: https://go/redwood/runbooks/project-affinity-fallback — i'll draft it.
Priya: for console rollout banner: "Project-affinity routing enabled for your org — learn more" with a link to opt-out per key for 7 days. legal/reg customers may need more control.
devinfra-bot: deploy queued: `canary-routing-v2` -> infra-canary-3 at 2023-08-31T16:02:00Z :rocket:
Tom: small nit — telemetry schema change should be backward compatible. add new fields with `routing_v2.*` prefix.
Liu: agree. also, log a single span event for `routing.decision` to avoid metrics explosion.
Jules: I'll sketch the metric names: `redwood.routing.decision{reason}`, `redwood.routing.fallback.count`, `redwood.routing.latency.millis`. add `pool.unavailable=true` dimension.
Asha: can someone volunteer to own the console opt-out UI and the admin audit trail for opt-outs? need an owner before EOD.
Priya: I'll take the console bits and audit trail.
Tom: i'll take telemetry schema + alerting.
Liu: i'll implement circuit breaker and the sampling toggles.
Jules: i'll wire up metric dashboards and add a kanban card for runbook remediation steps.
Asha: thanks. next steps: PRs for flags + schema by tomorrow morning, console mock by EOD. if blockers come up ping me @Asha. :thumbsup:
Priya: noted. adding tasks in the console epic.
Tom: one last thing — add a test in the integration suite that simulates pool failover and verifies `routing.reason=fallback-org`.
Liu: good call. will add test and load profile.
Asha: awesome. marking this thread as actioned.
